HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Living Room Words — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the living room without anyone standing up: the sofa is the classroom, and everything taught is within pointing distance.

What is this?

The living room is the gathering room: the sofa to sit on, the television to watch, the coffee table to rest a cup, the floor lamp for light, the remote control for the deciding.

What does it mean?

Children already own this room — naming its parts makes their favorite territory official. Vocabulary that attaches to comfort sticks faster than vocabulary that attaches to lessons.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and the sofa. Round one is five pointing answers from sitting down; round two is the swap-seats version, which refreshes the answers for free.

Why this matters

The living room is where families talk, so it is where family vocabulary pays off daily: put it on the coffee table, sit on the sofa, lamp on for reading.

What it teaches

Object naming in context, positional words (on, under, beside — where IS the remote?), and turn-taking in a seated game.

Words to learn

sofatelevisioncoffee tablefloor lampremote controlliving room

Say this to your child

“"Living room words — from the best seat in the house! Sofa under us, television there, lamp in the corner. Now — where is that remote hiding?"”

Step by step

  1. Sit on the sofa with the card: "this room has five names on it — let us find them from here."
  2. Point at each real thing: sofa (we are on it), television, coffee table, floor lamp, remote.
  3. Swap seats and name five again — the new view finds new details.
  4. Ask: "what does the remote do?" — one button press, together, then it rests.
  5. End with the lamp: switch it on for story time, and the room has a mood you made.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Living Room Words" sit over a blue sofa with cushions, a wide television, a round coffee table, a tall floor lamp and a remote control with many buttons.

Ask your child

"Where do we sit together?" (the sofa) "What rests our cups?" (the coffee table) "Who turned the lamp on just now?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might claim the remote seat as a throne, label the whole room aloud to a stuffed audience, or put the remote exactly where the card shows it.

Out in the real world

Every gathering place has a sofa-word and a screen-word — hotels, waiting rooms, grandparents. The child who names their living room names every living room.

Try it together

Remote Hunt: hide the remote (in plain sight — under the cushion, on the coffee table, beside the lamp) and give warm-and-cold clues. The finder presses one button as the prize. The room teaches itself while you play.

Understanding check

Ask: "Where are we sitting?" (the sofa) "What is the little table called?" (the coffee table) "What do we press to choose the show?" (the remote control)

This lesson pairs with the Living Room Words flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
